newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia corn market dips, awaits Soon Soon tender.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia corn market dips, awaits Soon Soon tender.

text.p: Prices of corn in Malaysia fell this week after being pressured by oversupply and the market's immediate focus was on a maize/soybean tender by Soon Soon Oilmills Sdn Bhd on Wednesday, traders said.
Stocks of maize in Malaysian warehouses totalled around 170,000 tonnes on Tuesday, after shortcovering by feedmillers reduced last week's volume of about 200,000 tonnes, they said.
"There's been some covering of about 30,000 tonnes by feedmills in the last week," said a trader with a flour mill.
Soon Soon Oilmills was expected to tender on Wednesday for a combined cargo of corn and soybeans totalling 55,000 tonnes for October shipment/November arrival, traders said.
"It's not really a key thing but there's little else happening," said another trader, explaining the interest in the oil mill tender.
A Soon Soon spokesman in Malaysia's northern Penang island declined to comment on the tender.
Traders said there were indications that ports taking in grains were facing congestion and this could delay new arrivals of corn and curb the growing stockpile.

Chinese bulk corn ex-factories/godowns in Malaysia's central region traded at 370 to 375 ringgit a tonne C & F this week, while an equal tonnage of South American material fetched between 380 and 385 ringgit.
Last week, maize prices were between 375 and 385 ringgit per tonne C & F on average.
Soymeal's price was maintained at 860 to 870 ringgit for imported material while local soymeal continued to fetch around 880 ringgit.
"A" grade wheat in bags was unchanged at 730 ringgit. "B" grade wheat was also steady at 430 ringgit.
